text: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be thankful to Me, and do not be ungrateful.
O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
Allah does not burden a soul with more than it can bear.
Truly, it is in the remembrance of Allah that hearts find rest.
If you are grateful, I will certainly give you more.
Whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for him, and provide for him from where he never expected.
So, surely with hardship comes ease. Surely with hardship comes ease.
Those who strive for Our sake, We will surely guide them to Our paths.
And establish the prayer for My remembrance.
Indeed, the prayer restrains one from indecency and wrongdoing.
Indeed, the prayer has been prescribed for the believers at fixed times.
Successful indeed are the believers — those who humble themselves in their prayer.
Seek help through patience and prayer. It is indeed hard, except for the humble.
By time — humanity is surely in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and counsel one another to truth and to patience.
In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, there are signs for people of understanding.
I did not create jinn and humankind except to worship Me.
When My servants ask you about Me — I am near. I answer the call of the caller when he calls on Me.
Your Lord has said: Call upon Me, and I will respond to you.
Eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not love those who are excessive.
The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they respond with peace.
The most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the most mindful of Him.
Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be good to your parents.
Whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah.
And once you have made a decision, put your trust in Allah.
Whoever puts his trust in Allah — He is sufficient for him.
Indeed, Allah loves those who turn to Him in repentance, and He loves those who keep themselves pure.
Do not despair of Allah's mercy. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.
Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer — We will surely grant them a good life.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
Is the reward for goodness anything but goodness?
O my son, establish the prayer, encourage what is good, forbid what is wrong, and be patient with whatever befalls you.
And in part of the night, pray with it as an extra offering for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.
And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening.
O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening.
And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
Allah will raise in rank those of you who believe and those who are given knowledge.
Cooperate with one another in righteousness and mindfulness of Allah, and do not cooperate in sin and transgression.
When you are greeted with a greeting, respond with something better, or at least return it.
Avoid much suspicion — some suspicion is sin. And do not spy, nor backbite one another.
Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love that Allah should forgive you?
Repel evil with what is better, and the one you had enmity with will become like a close friend.
We made your sleep a means of rest, made the night a covering, and made the day for earning a living.
Among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty.
When the prayer is over, disperse through the land and seek Allah's bounty, and remember Allah often, so that you may succeed.
O you who believe, eat from the good things We have provided you, and give thanks to Allah.
Do not squander your wealth wastefully. The wasteful are the brothers of devils.
And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be well pleased.
So when you have finished your task, devote yourself to worship, and turn to your Lord with longing.
Allah intends ease for you, and does not intend hardship for you.
O you who believe, be patient, outdo others in patience, remain steadfast, and be mindful of Allah, so that you may succeed.
If you support Allah's cause, He will support you and make your footsteps firm.
Whoever is patient and forgives — that is truly a matter of firm resolve.
And do good — indeed, Allah loves those who do good.
O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and stand with those who are truthful.
The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and whose faith increases when His verses are recited to them.
Recite what is easy for you of the Qur'an.
This is a blessed Book We have revealed to you, so that they may reflect on its verses.
Take provision, and the best provision is mindfulness of Allah.
Race one another towards forgiveness from your Lord.
Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.
The deeds most beloved to Allah are those done consistently, even if they are few.
Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will have what they intended.
The first thing a servant will be held accountable for on the Day of Judgement is the prayer.
Purity is half of faith.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or stay silent.
None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah's help, and do not give up.

Take advantage of five before five: your youth before your old age, your health before your illness, your wealth before your poverty, your free time before your busyness, and your life before your death.
There are two blessings that many people are deceived about: good health and free time.
Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise.
The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.
Whoever recites a single letter from the Book of Allah earns a good deed, and each good deed is multiplied by ten.
Two words light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdih, SubhanAllahil-'Azeem.
Whoever says 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdih' one hundred times a day will have his sins forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea.
Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.
Smiling in the face of your brother is an act of charity.
The best of you is the one who is best to his family, and I am the best of you to my family.
He is not one of us who shows no mercy to our young and no respect to our elders.
Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow a bad deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with good character.
Charity does not decrease wealth.

A person's feet will not move on the Day of Judgement until he is asked about his life and how he spent it, his knowledge and what he did with it, his wealth — how he earned it and how he spent it, and his body and how he used it.
No vessel is filled worse than the stomach. A few morsels are enough to keep a person's back straight. If more is needed, then a third for food, a third for drink, and a third for breath.
Whoever prays Fajr is under the protection of Allah.
Whoever prays the two cool prayers — Fajr and Asr — will enter Paradise.
The two units of prayer before Fajr are better than the world and everything in it.
Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of every night, saying: Who is calling on Me, that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me, that I may give him?
The closest a servant is to his Lord is while prostrating, so make plenty of supplication then.
Supplication is worship itself.
Whoever holds fast to seeking forgiveness, Allah will grant him relief from every worry, a way out of every hardship, and provision from where he never expected.
source: Sunan Abi Dawud 1518; Sunan Ibn Majah 3819

text: Do deeds properly and moderately, and know that none of you will enter Paradise by his deeds alone.
Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
Whoever relieves a believer of a hardship in this world, Allah will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection.
O Allah, bless my nation in its early mornings.
The believer who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently has a greater reward than the believer who does not.
Whoever wakes up secure in his home, healthy in body, with enough food for the day, it is as though the whole world has been given to him.
Richness is not having many possessions; true richness is contentment of the soul.
Whoever is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah.
The Prophet was asked which deed is best. He said: The prayer at its proper time. Then what? He said: Kindness to parents.
A good word is charity.
Removing something harmful from the road is charity.
Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.
Faith has over seventy branches. The highest is saying 'there is no god but Allah', the lowest is removing something harmful from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith.
Whoever guides someone to good will have a reward like the one who does it.
When a person dies, their deeds end except three: ongoing charity, knowledge others benefit from, and a righteous child who prays for them.
Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.
Whoever prays Isha in congregation is as though he prayed half the night, and whoever prays Fajr in congregation is as though he prayed the whole night.
Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you.
Tie your camel first, then put your trust in Allah.
Whoever would love for his provision to be increased and his life extended, let him keep good ties with his relatives.
Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times better than prayer offered alone.
A man asked the Prophet for advice. He said: Do not become angry. The man repeated his request, and he said: Do not become angry.
No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm or sadness afflicts a Muslim — even a thorn that pricks him — without Allah wiping away some of his sins by it.
How wonderful is the affair of the believer — all of it is good. If something good happens he is grateful, and that is good for him; if hardship strikes he is patient, and that is good for him.
Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times.
The best charity is what you give while healthy and tight-fisted, hoping for wealth and fearing poverty.
Whoever performs ablution well, his sins leave his body, even from beneath his fingernails.
Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and hoping for reward will have his previous sins forgiven.
Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need of him giving up his food and drink.
The most beloved places to Allah are the mosques, and the most disliked places to Allah are the markets.
Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will keep him chaste; whoever seeks to be self-sufficient, Allah will make him self-sufficient; and whoever is patient, Allah will grant him patience.
